newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine Q3 industrial output at 9.6 pct-official.
newsitem.headline: Argentine Q3 industrial output at 9.6 pct-official.

text.p: Argentina's industrial output grew at least 9.6 percent between July-September compared to the same period of 1995, Industry Secretary Alieto Guadagni said Wednesday.
He said third-quarter industrial production growth was only 1.9 percent slower than in the same period of 1994, which set a record for quarterly output since 1980.
"Argentina's economy is not going through a temporary reactivation, but has rather resumed the path of steady growth," Guadagni told a news conference.
He said economic recovery was powered by greater gross domestic investments and exports.
"Steady reactivation will help lower levels of unemployment and poverty which currently affect significant portions of the population," he said.
Argentina, which capped a 12-month recession in April, is still fighting 17.1 percent unemployment.
Private consultants FIEL said earlier on Wednesday that industrial production rose 9.7 percent in September compared to the same month last year, but dropped 3.7 percent from August.
Guadagni said according to official estimates, industrial output grew at least 8.5 percent in September. He said a fall from August could be blamed on a 36-hour general strike.
Guadagni also said by the end of the year Argentine exports will have soared 136 percent, or similar to the export growth rate of leading Pacific rim countries.
Foreign trade in the past three months totalled a record $13.2 billion, the official said.

He noted third-quarter imports rose 13.7 percent from the same period of 1994 and 34.3 percent from 1995, while exports rose 54 percent and 16.4 percent against the same quarters of 1994 and 1995, respectively.
